# The reported case's figures. A sale of 2,720.00 USD into a US dollar bank,
# stated in US dollars with its income split at 3,815.89 CAD, so the dollars'
# cost basis costs 381589/272000 CAD per USD. Three transactions then spend all
# 2,720.00 USD, each drawing on that cost basis:
#
#   0.72 USD, a bank charge of 1.00 CAD     exact cost 1.0100…, valued 1.01
#   8.60 USD, a bank charge of 11.92 CAD    exact cost 12.0649…, valued 12.06
#   2,710.68 USD, 3,758.36 CAD to chequing  the last, in a file of its own
#
# The last is ..._the_last_at_what_is_left.txt: valued at what is left of the
# cost basis's 3,815.89, 3,802.82, so the three values add up to what the
# dollars cost, and the exchange splits, 0.01 + 0.14 + 44.46, to the realized
# loss: 3,815.89 − 3,771.28 = 44.61.
#
# Or ..._the_last_at_its_own_share.txt: valued at its own share of the cost
# rounded, 3,802.81, as the reported book was. The three values then add up to
# 3,815.88, and the exchange splits to a realized loss of 44.60.
#
# A second sale of 1,020.00 USD at 1,413.82 CAD is still held, so a balance
# sheet at 1.4096 (fx_rates_usd_at_1_4096.yaml) states an unrealized gain.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_the_last_disposal_of_a_cost_basis_takes_what_is_left_of_its_cost.py and
# tests/integration/test_a_balance_sheet_states_the_realized_gain_the_book_did_not_record.py.
